title: Motion in a Straight Line

key_big: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as.
key_sub: Slope of x–t is v; slope of v–t is a; area under v–t is s.
body_html:
How to think about it

Displacement is the change of position; distance is the length of the path. Average velocity = displacement ÷ time, average speed = distance ÷ time. For uniform acceleration: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at² and v² = u² + 2as. In free fall a = g = 9.8 m/s² downwards.

On a position–time graph the slope is the velocity; on a velocity–time graph the slope is the acceleration and the area is the displacement. Relative velocity of B with respect to A is vB − vA.

Example

u = 0, a = 2 m/s², t = 5 s. Find s.

s = ½ × 2 × 25

Answer: 25 m

Example

Average speed: 30 km/h there, 60 km/h back?

2 × 30 × 60 ÷ 90

Answer: 40 km/h

Common mistakes

  • Taking the simple mean of two speeds over equal distances.
  • Saying acceleration is zero at the top of a throw.
  • Mixing up distance and displacement.

faq.q: What does the area under a v–t graph give?

faq.a: The velocity of one body as seen from another: v<sub>BA</sub> = v<sub>B</sub> − v<sub>A</sub>.
